title: Anne of Green Gables, L. M. Montgomery, Project Gutenberg 45
question: Compare the age Anne gives when she says how old she was last March with the age she gives while insisting on her plans near the end. What is the difference between these two stated ages in years? Give both statements as evidence.
original: I’m sixteen and a half, ‘obstinate as a
replacement: I’m sixteen and three quarters, ‘obstinate as a
rubric_original: Eleven last March; sixteen and a half in the later exchange. The difference between the stated ages is five and a half years.
rubric_edited: Eleven last March; sixteen and three quarters in the later exchange. The difference is five and three quarters years.
followup: Use the calculator to express the difference you found in months. Show which two ages you used.
unanswerable: At precisely which clock minute did Anne make the later age statement? If the text doesn't give a minute, say so.
order: Use the complete original edition or single documented edit. The calculator is available from the first turn. The follow-up requires a live successful arithmetic callback and the correct final answer using the source ages; record own and common first-answer histories separately.
